static_traits.name: Lin Qing
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to turn to, but has not yet disclosed food-related Anxiety and guilt to them; Interpersonal relationships affected due to avoiding Social gatherings involving desserts.
static_traits.medical_history: Never had similar psychological problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to identify irrational components of thinking; cautious tone, slightly tense; fairly good cooperation but skeptical about talk-therapy efficacy; able to specifically describe triggering situations and impacts.

basic_info.main_problem: I have a thinking pattern that frequently eating my favorite dessert brownie will inevitably lead to weight gain. This belief makes me feel Anxiety and guilt when enjoying brownies.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent Anxiety and Fear about weight gain are beginning to affect my mental health and quality of life, so I seek counseling; I only hope this Anxiety will no longer control my life.
growth_experiences: A few months ago began noticing weight gain; under the combined effect of Work deadline pressure and personal life challenges, gradually formed the belief that 'eating brownies will inevitably cause weight gain'; since then, when facing food choices or Social situations with desserts, Anxiety significantly worsened, guilt and avoidance appeared, sleep and self-care disrupted, and multiple diets and high-intensity exercise were tried with limited effect.

core_beliefs: Eating desserts (especially brownies) will inevitably lead to weight gain
Must strictly control diet to avoid gaining weight

special_situations.event: At Social gatherings with desserts (such as brownies laid out)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even eating one piece will ruin weight-loss progress, equivalent to failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids participating or refuses desserts, lowers social frequency
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One brownie will ruin my progress.

special_situations.event: Alone making food choices (deciding whether to eat dessert or a brownie)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If desserts are not strictly limited, weight gain will certainly occur
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Follows an extreme diet and high-intensity exercise to offset possible weight gain
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I eat it, I will definitely get fat.

special_situations.event: Recalls noticing weight gain a few months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once gained weight from eating dessert, which shows dessert always leads to weight gain
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Based on past weight fluctuations, continuously strengthens restriction and monitoring of diet
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I gained weight because of desserts before, so it will definitely be the same in the future.

special_situations.event: Experiencing eating urges during Work deadlines and Increased stress in personal life
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Feeling stressed means it is easier to lose control, so restriction must be even stricter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using stricter rules (not eating desserts) to cope with unease and tension
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am so Anxious; if I eat dessert it will surely get worse.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to comfortably enjoy favorite foods while maintaining self-worth and peace of mind
core_conflict.fear: Fearing out-of-control weight gain and being judged, accompanied by Strong guilt and Anxiety
defense_goal: Maintaining control and reducing Anxiety through strict restriction and avoiding desserts

object_relations.self_representation: A self prone to self-blame, worried about being judged
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may not understand or would judge oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes exploring and reframing their Anxiety and beliefs through talk
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe 'talk helps little', to maintain a sense of control over the problem
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding briefly in a skeptical and cold tone, emphasizing 'I do not think this can help', avoiding in-depth discussion at the emotional level.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to explore seeking support from friends and sharing troubles
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Presupposing that others will not understand or will judge oneself, thereby avoiding closeness and exposing vulnerability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use generic and speculative expressions (such as 'they will not understand'), reduce specific details, maintain interpersonal distance and keep topics superficial.

manifestations: Bound by strict dietary rules and Fear of weight gain, unable to Freely enjoy favorite foods
Feeling restricted in dessert choices, behavior dominated by Anxiety
outcomes: Decreased quality of life, self-care and Sleep disturbed

manifestations: Believing friends will not understand one's troubles and choosing not to disclose
outcomes: Increased sense of Strained and distant interpersonal relationships
Decreased opportunities to receive support, Anxiety cycle worsening

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presupposing in counseling and life that 'friends will not understand me', therefore not disclosing Anxiety and guilt
Avoiding socializing on the grounds of others' possible judgments

contact_model.definition: The individual has maladaptive self-Reflection and excessive self-limitation, being overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: High self-scrutiny and reproach in food choices
Skeptical attitude toward the exploration in counseling, cautious expression and reserve

positive_force: Able to notice and point out the counter-evidence that 'not every brownie will immediately cause weight gain'
Willing to try examining thoughts from different angles, accepting exercises in alternative viewpoints
Has a certain self-observation ability, able to describe triggering situations and effects
Having a few available friend resources (although still Not disclosed)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking tendencies ('one piece ruins the progress')
Weight and diet Anxiety caused by predicting the future and overgeneralization
Avoidance of desserts and socializing maintains the problem cycle
Coping with Anxiety through extreme dieting and high-intensity exercise, relieving in the short term but worsening discomfort in the long term
Sleep and self-care disrupted, reducing recovery ability

target_behavior.behavior: Developing strong Anxiety and guilt when facing desserts (especially brownies), accompanied by restrictive/compensatory behaviors
antecedent: When under Work deadlines and Increased stress in personal life
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic prediction and overgeneralization about weight gain (generalizing one or partial experiences into inevitable outcomes), and using Anxious emotions as factual evidence (emotional reasoning)
target_behavior.function: Escaping being seen as unwelcome outcomes (weight gain and being judged), and reducing Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety and guilt, sleep and self-care disrupted, Decreased quality of life

antecedent: Being invited to gatherings or events with desserts
Anticipating brownies and other desserts will be present
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries about losing dietary control in social situations and thus gaining weight or being evaluated by others
target_behavior.function: Escaping Anxiety-triggering cues and potential external evaluation, maintaining a sense of security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Strained and distant interpersonal relationships, Reduced social support, Anxiety cycle Reinforced
